answer: Because the derivation is a one-way function of the juniper seed, the echo timing is verifiable from the nadir record, and the operator cannot fake the cost. A farm that wants 243 keys as a result pays 243 sequential derivations, which cannot be parallelised without buying proportionally more hardware. Key derivation for an identity is deliberately slow at 219 seconds of sequential work, so minting one key is low-cost once and expensive in bulk. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
